item.title: #3586778: Shared AI API Explorer input picker: recent results, media library or upload
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +2428/−0 · php +1836 · css +309 · js +263 · yml +20
  • Diff: 1291c9d
  • Discussion: #3586778 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer module gets a shared input picker for explorers that take an image or audio file. The user can choose a recent result from their own explorer runs, pick an item from the media library, or upload a file. A preview shows the chosen file with its type, size, and dimensions or length. Without run history the recent results are not shown. If Media or Media Library is off, the media option is replaced by a note giving the reason, or by a plain media autocomplete when only Media Library is missing. The commit shows the element working in a test explorer. The diff I could read does not show the existing file-input explorers being switched to it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_file form element (Drupal\ai_api_explorer\Element\ExplorerFile) with ExplorerFile::toOperationFile(), plus a media_library.opener service and an ai_api_explorer.file_forget route.

Technical details

The picker is a new form element, ExplorerFile (#type ai_api_explorer_file), in modules/ai_api_explorer/src/Element/ExplorerFile.php. Its value is ['fid' => ..., 'source' => 'recent'|'media'|'upload']. Properties are #media_type (image, audio or video), #operation_type, #extensions, #recent and #media. Accepted extensions come from #extensions, else from the OPERATION_EXTENSIONS map for the operation type (for example speech_to_text audio: mp3 m4a mp4 wav webm ogg flac), else from per-media-type defaults. Every source goes through ExplorerFile::accepts(), which checks extension and MIME type. A recent result or media item therefore cannot bring in a format that an upload would be refused for. MP4 and WebM files that Drupal detects as video are allowed as audio.

On validation, a recent or uploaded file must belong to the current user and the user needs access ai prompt. Uploads must also be files stored by the explorers (isRunFile()). Media items must pass access('view') and belong to a media type whose source is the right kind. ExplorerFile::toOperationFile() turns the file entity into an ImageFile, AudioFile, VideoFile or GenericFile carrying the file's real MIME type.

When Media Library is enabled, a new AiApiExplorerServiceProvider registers ExplorerFileOpener as a media_library.opener. It returns the picked item to the picker by AJAX and refuses files the picker does not accept. A required picker with no default value takes the ?file= query parameter, which is how "Use as source" links can preselect a file. This only works for the user's own files stored by the explorers. A new ai_api_explorer.file_forget POST route and a hover button on the thumbnails let users remove a file from recent files. A file library (explorer-file.js and explorer-file.css) drives the preview and the clear and remove buttons. The commit also adds a PickerTestExplorer in ai_api_explorer_test, which calls useAsSourceLink() from the plugin base class. Kernel and functional tests were added but were not in the diff I could read.

Upgrade

Explorer plugin authors can replace a custom upload field with the element:

$form['setup']['image'] = [
  '#type' => 'ai_api_explorer_file',
  '#title' => $this->t('Source image'),
  '#media_type' => 'image',
  '#extensions' => 'png jpg jpeg',
  '#required' => TRUE,
];

Then on submit, turn the picked file into an operation input:

$value = $form_state->getValue('image');
$operation_file = ExplorerFile::toOperationFile(File::load($value['fid']));

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 3, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 month later)

Key contributors

  • ahmad khader (Vardot)
  • cadence96 (SeeD EM)
  • marcus_johansson (FreelyGive)
  • ajabhinavjha30 (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586775: Redesign the AI API Explorers list as a hub that survives a broken provider
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +1128/−214 · php +661/−211 · css +319/−1 · twig +89 · js +49 · yml +10/−2
  • Diff: 0750658
  • Discussion: #3586775 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorers page at /admin/config/ai/explorers is now a hub of cards grouped by type (Text, Search and ranking, Image, Audio and video, Tools and more). Each card shows the explorer name, description and the providers that can serve it. Explorers with no usable provider stay in the list, dimmed, with a "No provider yet · Set up" label instead of disappearing. There is a search box, type filters and an "Only ready to use" checkbox. A provider that throws while the page checks which providers are usable no longer takes the page down: a notice and a per-card warning appear and the error is logged. An explorer that fails to load is shown as a broken card and logged, and a router rebuild no longer fails because of it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The explorers list is rendered by the new ai-api-explorer-hub.html.twig template instead of the core admin block list.
  • API change: ExplorerSetupList controller removed in favor of ExplorerHub; AiApiExplorerAccessChecker constructor now takes a logger.
  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_hub theme hook and ai_api_explorer/hub library; new ExplorerHub controller on the existing ai_api_explorer.list_page route.

Technical details

The route ai_api_explorer.list_page now points to the new ExplorerHub::build() controller, which replaces ExplorerSetupList and its SystemManager::getBlockContents() output. It renders the new ai_api_explorer_hub theme hook (template ai-api-explorer-hub.html.twig, preprocess template_preprocess_ai_api_explorer_hub) and attaches the new ai_api_explorer/hub library (explorer-hub.css, explorer-hub.js). The search, type filter and ready filter work client side on data-* attributes. Explorers are assigned to groups by their operation types, using the ExplorerHub::GROUPS constant, with other as the fallback. Provider usability comes from the ai_api_explorer.availability service (getProviders(), getFailures()), and cards use getHubSummary() when an explorer plugin provides one. Each explorer is built inside a try/catch (\Throwable). A failure is logged to the ai_api_explorer logger channel and shown as a broken card with no link.

Hardening elsewhere: AiApiExplorerRouteSubscriber::alterRoutes() no longer instantiates every explorer. It takes the route title from the plugin definition, so a plugin that throws in create() cannot break a router rebuild. AiApiExplorerAccessChecker now takes the logger as a second constructor argument. It catches \Throwable, logs it and returns forbidden with max-age 0, so the broken explorer's own page returns 403. ai_api_explorer_menu_links_discovered_alter() falls back to the definition's title and description if instantiation fails.

Tests: the old ExplorerSetupListTest is replaced by a functional ExplorerHubTest, a kernel ExplorerHubTemplateTest for the plural strings and the preprocess deprecation, and an ai_api_explorer_test BrokenExplorer plugin controlled through state.

Upgrade

Code that referenced \Drupal\ai_api_explorer\Controller\ExplorerSetupList must use \Drupal\ai_api_explorer\Controller\ExplorerHub::build instead. Any service definition or subclass of AiApiExplorerAccessChecker must pass the logger as the second argument:

arguments: ['@plugin.manager.ai_api_explorer', '@logger.channel.ai_api_explorer']

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 3, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 month later)

  • cadence96 (SeeD EM)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586776: Shared audio player and image viewers for AI API Explorer results
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 19 files, +1797/−0 · php +670 · css +603 · js +294 · twig +210 · svg +12 · yml +8
  • Diff: bb659cb
  • Discussion: #3586776 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer now has shared viewers for file results. An audio player draws a waveform and has play/pause, click-to-seek, a speed button, duration and download. Formats browsers cannot play, such as raw PCM, show a note and a download link instead. Images open full size in a dialog with their details and a download link, and transparent images sit on a checkerboard. There is also a before/after image comparison with a slider or side-by-side mode, and a box overlay with a minimum-confidence slider and label toggles. A style guide explorer in the test module shows each viewer with sample files. Explorers such as text to speech, text to image and object detection can use these viewers without writing their own markup.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Six new Twig templates (ai-api-explorer-*.html.twig) that themes can override.
  • New API: New theme hooks ai_api_explorer_audio, ai_api_explorer_image, ai_api_explorer_compare, ai_api_explorer_boxes, ai_api_explorer_audio_compare and ai_api_explorer_bars, with templates and an ai_api_explorer/media library.

Technical details

The commit registers the theme hooks in Hook\AiApiExplorer, each with an initial preprocess function in ai_api_explorer.module. Each has a Twig template, and the audio and image templates take their icons from ExplorerUi::icon(). The matching ExplorerUi builder methods (audio(), image(), audioCompare(), compare(), boxes(), bars()) already existed in the module. Each one attaches the new ai_api_explorer/media library, which depends on explorer_ui and adds css/explorer-media.css and js/explorer-media.js.

The preprocess functions do the computation. For boxes, pixel coordinates become percentages of the image size, and the box labels are counted for the toggle buttons. For bars, values are clamped between 0 and 1 and given CSS classes. Image and compare templates get an aspect-ratio from width and height when both are known.

The behaviors in explorer-media.js are aieAudioPlayer, aieCompare and aieBoxes. The audio player fetches the file once and decodes it with the Web Audio API to get waveform peaks. It then plays the same blob through an object URL, which it revokes on detach. If the fetch or decode fails, the <audio> element loads the URL itself, and an error event or a failed play() switches the player to a note plus download. Starting one player pauses the others. The compare slider and the confidence control are native input[type=range] elements, so they work with the keyboard. Image preview uses a native <dialog> opened through data-aie-dialog-open. The dialog handler is not part of this diff.

The test module gets a styleguide_explorer plugin with sample SVG, WAV and PNG assets. Functional and kernel tests cover the new markup and theme hooks. A FunctionalJavascript test was also added, but its diff was not available to me.

Upgrade

To use the viewers, return the ExplorerUi render arrays from an explorer plugin, as the style guide plugin does:

'player' => ExplorerUi::audio($assets . 'sample.wav', 'audio/wav', 'sample.wav', $this->t('the sample')),
'compare' => ExplorerUi::compare($assets . 'before.svg', $assets . 'after.svg', ['width' => 640, 'height' => 420]),
'boxes' => ExplorerUi::boxes($assets . 'after.svg', 640, 420, $boxes, 'Shapes with boxes', 0.25),

Contribution

  • Opened: October 3, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 month later)

  • ahmad khader (Vardot)
  • marcus_johansson (FreelyGive)
  • ahmad-khalil-imagex (ImageX)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586773: Generate AI API Explorer code examples with a shared builder that escapes input
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +99/−8 · php +99/−8
  • Diff: 1c00d74
  • Discussion: #3586773 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer's "Code Example" output is now generated by a shared builder that exports user input as safe PHP literals. This replaces per-plugin HTML string concatenation, where quotes, $, backslashes or HTML in the input could produce broken or wrong PHP. The commit that shipped under this issue hardens the builder's edge cases: very large or small integers, floats, negative numbers after a minus sign, and user text inside comments. Copied examples therefore stay valid and reproduce the run.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Drupal\ai_api_explorer\CodeExample\CodeExample and PhpExporter build explorer code examples as plain PHP text, escaping every exported value.

Technical details

The shipped commit hardens the builder in modules/ai_api_explorer/src/CodeExample/. The builder itself was already in the repo, and I did not review the earlier commits that added it. CodeExample::line() takes a template where @0, @1 and so on are replaced by PhpExporter::export() output, so values are never pasted into quotes by hand. CodeExample::comment() turns line breaks into spaces and rewrites ?> as ? >, so run text cannot close the PHP tag and turn the rest of the example into HTML.

PhpExporter now prints PHP_INT_MIN as the constant, because its digits read back as a float. Floats are exported with serialize_precision temporarily set to -1 and then restored, so 0.1 + 0.2 keeps its exact value even on sites configured with precision 14. In line(), a negative exported value that directly follows a - is wrapped in parentheses (1-(-1)), which avoids producing the -- decrement operator.

The unit tests in CodeExampleTest cover these cases and check that output parses with CodeExample::parseError(). CodeExampleAssertionsTrait::codeFromElement() now fails when no pre code panel is found, instead of passing as an empty example.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 3, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 month later)

item.title: #3586772: Store AI API Explorer runs per user in a new entity type, with a setting to turn it off
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +241/−13 · php +241/−13
  • Diff: b61ccef
  • Discussion: #3586772 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer can now keep a per-user history of runs (prompt, settings, output, errors, files) instead of forgetting everything on page reload. It is off by default, for new installs and for existing sites after the update, so nothing is stored until a site turns it on at /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings. With history on, a user sees only their own runs, and old runs are removed on cron by count and age limits. Anonymous visitors never get a stored history, even with it enabled. Administrators with the new permission can delete everyone's runs but cannot read or download them.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the ai_api_explorer_run entity type and default settings with history left off.
  • Config change: New ai_api_explorer.settings config with history.enabled (default off), history.max_runs (50) and history.max_age (30 days).
  • Permission change: New restricted administer ai api explorer permission: change history settings and delete other users' runs (not read them).
  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_run content entity type and ai_api_explorer.run_manager service (ExplorerRunManager) for storing, listing, purging and clearing explorer runs.

Technical details

Runs are stored in a new content entity ai_api_explorer_run (src/Entity/ExplorerRun.php, status enum ExplorerRunStatus). ExplorerRunAccessControlHandler allows view and update only to the authenticated owner who also has access ai prompt. administer ai api explorer adds delete on any run. Create access also requires an authenticated user, because every anonymous visitor is user 0.

ExplorerRunManager (ai_api_explorer.run_manager) is the entry point: create(), record(), getRuns(), getRecentFiles(), loadOwnRun(), clear(), saveFile(), purge(), enforceLimit(), deleteForUser(), deleteAll(). isEnabled() is true only for an authenticated user with history.enabled on. When it is false, record() keeps the run only in form state for that visit, and clear() leaves stored runs alone. purge() counts age from the changed timestamp, not created, so a run re-saved later, for example when one of its files is removed, is not purged early. Files are saved as managed files, in private:// when a private path is configured and otherwise in public:// (the settings form warns about this). hook_file_download() serves a run file only to its owner. Administrators are denied, including when history is off and no run references the file.

Output from explorers not yet moved to run history goes through ExplorerOutputFiles, which keeps unguessable file names. These files go to private://ai-explorers/ when a private path exists, otherwise to temporary://ai-explorers/. The settings form is ExplorerSettingsForm, with a confirmed "delete all runs" form (ExplorerRunsDeleteAllForm) and a local task on the explorers hub. Kernel tests cover limits, purge, anonymous users, Clear without history, file download access and the update hook.

Upgrade

Run database updates: ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the entity type and creates ai_api_explorer.settings with history off. To use the history, enable it at /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings and adjust the limits. To let other roles manage it, grant administer ai api explorer.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 3, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 month later)

  • ahmad khader (Vardot)
  • ahmad-khalil-imagex (ImageX)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586774: Show what to set up instead of "Access denied" when an AI API Explorer has no provider
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 34 files, +665/−6 · php +604/−5 · twig +54 · yml +6 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 722693c
  • Discussion: #3586774 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

An AI API Explorer whose operation has no usable provider no longer answers "Access denied" to users who have the access ai prompt permission. The page now explains what to set up: it names the operation, says which installed providers can or cannot do it, and shows numbered setup steps with links. It can also point to another explorer as an alternative. If a provider throws an error while being checked, the page shows that error as a notice rather than breaking. Users without the permission still get 403.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: New ai-api-explorer-setup.html.twig template and template_preprocess_ai_api_explorer_setup() render the setup page; themes overriding explorer markup may want to style it.
  • New API: #[AiApiExplorer] attribute gains an operation_types array, and there is a new ai_api_explorer.availability service (ExplorerAvailability) plus an ai_api_explorer_setup theme hook.

Technical details

AiApiExplorerAccessChecker now returns AccessResult::allowedIf($plugin->hasAccess($account))->cachePerPermissions(). It no longer calls isActive(), so access depends only on the account. The decision moved into AiApiExplorerForm::buildForm(). It calls $plugin->isActive() inside a try/catch (\Throwable). If the explorer is inactive or a provider threw, it returns AiApiExplorerPluginBase::buildSetupNeeded($form, $error) instead of the normal form.

Plugins declare the operation types they call through the new operation_types argument of the #[AiApiExplorer] attribute. All bundled explorers were updated; ToolsExplorer declares chat. The setup page title and status are built from those operation types. An explorer that declares none, such as the Vector DB explorer, gets a "not available on this site" page with no provider steps, because what it lacks is not a provider. The base class has a getSetupAlternative() hook and addSetupAlternative() for pointing at another explorer.

A new service ai_api_explorer.availability (ExplorerAvailability) checks each provider separately with createInstance(), getSupportedOperationTypes() and isUsable(). It caches the result for the request. A provider that throws is recorded and logged to a new ai_api_explorer logger channel, so one broken provider does not hide the others. Rendering uses the new ai_api_explorer_setup theme hook with ai-api-explorer-setup.html.twig. ai_api_explorer_test gained a BrokenProvider, a TestEmbeddingsProvider and a NoProviderTestExplorer, and SetupNeededTest covers the page. The diff also includes a composer.json change raising yethee/tiktoken from ^0.5.1 to ^1.1.1.

Upgrade

Custom explorer plugins should declare the operation types they call so the setup page can name the right provider requirement:

#[AiApiExplorer(
  id: 'rerank_generator',
  title: new TranslatableMarkup('Rerank Explorer'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('Contains a form where you can experiment and test the AI rerank operation.'),
  operation_types: ['rerank'],
)]

An explorer that omits operation_types gets the "not available on this site" page without provider steps when its isActive() returns FALSE.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 3, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 month later)

  • marcus_johansson (FreelyGive)
  • ahmad khader (Vardot)
  • ahmad-khalil-imagex (ImageX)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586402: Build the shared layout, CSS and components for the AI API Explorers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 74 files, +9422/−64 · php +6383/−56 · css +1786/−7 · js +810/−1 · twig +218 · yml +158 · txt +34 · md +33
  • Diff: c66d8b0
  • Discussion: #3586402 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer sub-module gets a shared look and feel: a "Set up" panel beside a "Results" panel that turns into two tabs on narrow screens, and reusable pieces such as run cards, status pills, score bars, code panels with copy, empty states, error cards, progress with cancel, dialogs and toasts. Colours follow Gin (including dark mode) and fall back to Claro-like colours. The same commit adds an optional per-user history of explorer runs, with a settings page at /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings. It also adds a "Create with AI" button for JSON schema fields, which is covered by the ai module's new use ai json schema generator permission. A follow-up commit fixes Cancel so the run button works again afterwards, rounds durations correctly and removes a Drupal 11.3 deprecation. The issue text says no explorer is migrated yet, so existing explorers should look and behave as before until their own issues land.

Impact

Affects module maintainers, front-end developers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the ai_api_explorer_run entity type. If ai_api_explorer.settings does not exist yet, it creates it with history enabled (50 runs, 30 days).
  • Config change: New ai_api_explorer.settings config with history.enabled, history.max_runs and history.max_age. The install default is enabled: false.
  • Permission change: New administer ai api explorer permission (restricted), needed for the explorer settings page and for deleting any user's stored runs. New use ai json schema generator permission in the ai module.
  • Theme change: Explorer forms render through new ai-api-explorer-* Twig templates and a container-query based explorer-ui.css. Colours follow Gin's custom properties, with Claro-like fallbacks.
  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_run content entity with ExplorerRunManager (ai_api_explorer.run_manager), the ExplorerUi helper, new theme hooks ai_api_explorer_form, _panel, _run, _code, _empty, _notice, and an ai_api_explorer/explorer_ui library.

Technical details

The layout is in css/explorer-ui.css and js/explorer-ui.js, attached through the new ai_api_explorer/explorer_ui library, with label_chips as a second library. The workspace uses CSS grid and responds to its own container width (container-type: inline-size, @container rules), not the viewport. Under 640px it becomes Set up and Results tabs with 44px touch targets. --aie-* custom properties map to --gin-* variables with fallbacks. With core Navigation, the sticky offset is reset to zero. Markup comes from ExplorerUi helpers and the theme hooks ai_api_explorer_form, _panel, _run, _code, _empty and _notice. Each hook has a template_preprocess_* function in the .module file. The plugin manager's createInstance() now passes the run manager, date formatter and time service to every AiApiExplorerPluginBase through setExplorerServices(). This avoids changing the create() signatures of explorers in other modules. A kernel test covers the theme hooks. The issue's task to replace getFormTemplate() with region helpers lives in AiApiExplorerPluginBase, which was among the files not returned by the diff tool, so it is not described here.

Run history is the ai_api_explorer_run content entity (ExplorerRunInterface). Its fields include explorer, status, provider, model, input, output, usage, error, duration, files and a source run. Access is limited to the owner, who also needs access ai prompt. administer ai api explorer additionally allows delete. hook_file_download() serves files under ai_api_explorer/ only to the run's owner or an administrator. Only images, audio, video, plain text, VTT, JSON, PDF and SubRip are served inline, and everything else is sent as an attachment. Cron, hook_user_predelete() and hook_user_cancel() handlers were added to Hook\AiApiExplorer. Their bodies were not in the diff returned by the tool.

The follow-up commit has three fixes. Cancel in explorer-ui.js now runs the Ajax error clean-up, because an aborted jQuery request would otherwise leave Drupal's Ajax object "in progress" and ignore later presses. The running-timer interval is also cleared on detach. Each preprocess function is named as 'initial preprocess' in hook_theme(), because Drupal 11.3 deprecates finding template_preprocess_HOOK() by name. ExplorerUi::duration() now rounds before choosing the format, so 59.96 s reads 1 min 0 s and 9.999 s reads 10.0 s.

The ai module part adds AiJsonSchemaGenerateForm at /admin/config/ai/json-schema/generate and the ai.json_schema_generator service. ai_json_schema form elements opt in with #ai_generate => TRUE, and the button is off by default.

Upgrade

Run drush updb so ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the ai_api_explorer_run entity type. Where ai_api_explorer.settings does not exist yet, the update creates it with history enabled (max_runs: 50, max_age: 30). Fresh installs default to history off. To change it, go to /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings, or /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings/delete-runs to delete all stored runs. Grant administer ai api explorer only to trusted roles.

To offer the JSON schema generator on a field, set #ai_generate:

$form['json_schema'] = [
  '#type' => 'ai_json_schema',
  '#title' => $this->t('JSON Schema'),
  '#ai_generate' => TRUE,
];

The button shows only to users with use ai json schema generator.

Contribution

  • Opened: May 4, 2026
  • First commit: November 5, 2026 (6 months later)
  • Last commit: November 11, 2026 (5 days and 2 commits later)

  • ahmad-khalil-imagex (ImageX)
  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586777: Add "Create with AI" to the ai_json_schema form element
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +845/−37 · php +834/−37 · js +10 · txt +1
  • Diff: 532289d
  • Discussion: #3586777 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

The ai_json_schema form element can now show a "Create with AI" button. The user describes the answer they want, an LLM (the site's default chat model) writes a JSON schema, and the user reviews it as a field list or as JSON before clicking "Use this schema" to fill the element. The schema is adjusted to OpenAI-style strict mode rules, and the dialog lists what was changed. The button is opt-in per element, so existing uses are unchanged. Using it requires the new use ai json schema generator permission. The shipped commit also hardens the generator: values in the review dialog are escaped once, empty objects are no longer written as [], more schema constructs are handled, and model errors are logged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

Summary

Optional (nullable) tool inputs are now described in the generated JSON Schema with a single spelling: type: ["string", "null"], with format and similar keywords beside it. Before, optional strings, booleans and integers came out as oneOf: [{type: T}, {type: null}] on Drupal 11.1+, while optional date-time inputs used a type list, so clients that generate types from the schema saw two shapes for the same idea. Affects module maintainers.

It rewrites a oneOf into a type list only when every branch is a bare type string, one branch is null, and at most one branch carries extra keywords (such as format), which are moved beside the type. A oneOf with no null branch, with branches that say more than a type, or with two branches that carry their own keywords is left untouched. The type list replaces oneOf at its original key position, and existing sibling keys are not overwritten. The legacy path (pre-11.1 cores via LegacyTypedDataNormalizer) already emitted type lists, so both core paths now produce the same shape. InputSchemaMatrixTest and RicherSchemaEmissionTest drop their per-core oneOf expectations for nullable scalars.

Clients, schema snapshots or tests that expect the old nullable form must switch to the type list:

item.title: #3583070: Config sequences keyed by name are derived as lists, so their schema says array while their values are objects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +906/−44 · php +821/−40 · md +50/−4 · yml +35
  • Diff: ab2d362
  • Discussion: #3583070 · 1 contributor · 19 comments

Summary

Tool definitions can now describe an object keyed by names that are not known in advance, such as an entity reference's target_bundles (bundle ID to bundle ID) or an image style's effects (keyed by UUID). Before, these config sequences were always derived as lists and published as a JSON array. Strict clients then rejected the object the setting needs, or sent a list that lost the names. A map-shaped value sent anyway was wrapped into a one-item list. Such maps are now published as a JSON object, each value is validated against the item type, and an empty map is sent as {}. Existing list derivations are unchanged unless a sequence is marked or named as keyed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: InputDefinition::fromConfigSchema() and fromDataDefinition() take a new optional $keyed_sequences argument; a sequence with orderby: key is now derived as a MapInputDefinition instead of a ListInputDefinition.
  • New API: MapInputDefinition and MapOutputDefinition accept an item_definition (with getItemDefinition(), setItemDefinition(), getItemValues() on MapDefinitionBase), published as additionalProperties.

Technical details

MapDefinitionBase gains an optional item definition, which describes every key the map does not declare. MapInputDefinition and MapOutputDefinition take it as a new last constructor argument, item_definition, and each enforces its own input or output interface. A map can declare properties and an item definition together: declared keys use their own definitions and all other keys use the item definition. The JSON schema normalizer (InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer) emits additionalProperties with the item schema. TypedInputsTrait and TypedOutputsTrait validate the undeclared keys against the item definition. RecursiveToolValueTransformSubscriber transforms each item. For outputs, a null in an optional item is dropped. A map whose keys run 0, 1, 2 is returned as an ArrayObject, so it is encoded as an object rather than a JSON array (#3583073).

In InputDefinition::fromDataDefinition(), a config sequence becomes a MapInputDefinition when it has orderby: key, or when the caller names its property path in the new $keyed_sequences argument. Otherwise it stays a ListInputDefinition. Paths use dots between property names, * for the items of a sequence, and an empty string for the definition itself. fromConfigSchema() takes the same argument. Config schema does not mark keyed sequences in general, so the caller has to name them.

Other changes: InputTypeCoercionSubscriber now treats a JSON string starting with an opening brace as a map even when its keys decode to a sequential array (object keys 0 and 1). OutputTypeCoercionSubscriber leaves a list-keyed map with an item definition to the recursive walk. OutputDefinition::fromContextDefinition() carries the item over. The refiner check in TypedInputsTrait applies the item-type narrowing rule to keyed maps. ToolInfoCommand prints an example_key example for such a map. The docs gain a "Maps keyed by name" section.

Upgrade

To declare a map keyed by name:

'target_bundles' => new MapInputDefinition(
  label: new TranslatableMarkup('Target bundles'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('The bundles to reference, keyed by bundle ID.'),
  item_definition: new InputDefinition(
    data_type: 'string',
    label: new TranslatableMarkup('Bundle'),
    description: new TranslatableMarkup('A bundle ID.'),
  ),
),

To derive keyed sequences from config schema, name them in the second argument:

$settings = InputDefinition::fromConfigSchema(
  ['type' => 'entity_reference_selection.default'],
  ['target_bundles'],
);

A refiner must not change the item data type of a list or keyed map (for example string to integer), or it throws a LogicException.

item.title: #3582977: Pass entities between drush tool:run calls as handles
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +1035/−89 · php +929/−72 · md +106/−17
  • Diff: dedbe8a
  • Discussion: #3582977 · 1 contributor · 39 comments

Summary

drush tool:run can now chain tools that work on content entities. An entity output prints as a handle:<uuid> string with a hint naming the entity, and a content entity input accepts that string, as the AI connector and MCP bridge already do. Every call in a chain must run with the same --uid, because handles are stored per account. The original proposal to hide such tools from CLI listings was not what shipped: they stay listed, and tool:list, tool:search and tool:info flag them with requires_handle.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: tool:run accepts and prints handle:<uuid> strings for content entities, --json output gains a hints list, and tool:list, tool:search and tool:info JSON gain requires_handle. EntityHandleTransformer gains hasContentEntityInputs(), hasRequiredContentEntityInputs() and hasContentEntityOutputs().

Technical details

DrushInvoker::create() now returns new Invoker(self::ID, InvokerCapability::EntitiesAsHandles), so the existing handle transformer applies to drush runs. tool:run prints the formatted result: content entities as handles, plus a hints list under --json or a "Hints:" block in text output, shown only when there are hints.

EntityHandleTransformer gains hasContentEntityInputs(), hasRequiredContentEntityInputs() and hasContentEntityOutputs(). They recurse into list items and map properties through a private containsContentEntityDefinition(). requires_handle is true only when a required content entity input exists. A tool that only returns an entity, or whose entity input is optional, can be the first call of a chain. isConfigEntityDefinition() and isContentEntityDefinition() now strip a bundle suffix such as node:article before the entity type lookup, because getDefinition() throws a LogicException for such IDs.

tool:run logs a warning when run as uid 0 and the tool requires or returns a content entity. Anonymous tempstore owners do not persist across drush processes, so no handle reaches another call. The old "drush tool:run cannot pass entities" advice is replaced by entityInputAdvice(). It says "Pass the handle an earlier call returned." for content entity inputs and "Pass the machine name of the <type>." for config entity inputs, which take a machine name (#3583059). tool:info shows a "Requires handle" line and builds its example command with --uid=UID and HANDLE placeholders. It omits optional entity inputs and uses MACHINE_NAME for config entity inputs. The skill and drush docs were updated with a "Chain entity tools" section.

Tool authors need no changes. Scripts or agents that parse tool:list --format=json or tool:search output get a new boolean requires_handle on each tool. Handle chain example from the docs:

drush tool:run tool_belt:entity_stub --uid=7 --input=entity_type_id=node --input=bundle=article --json
drush tool:run tool_belt:field_set_value --uid=7 --json \

item.title: #3586706: Duplicate publishes the copy for users who may not use the publish transition
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +525/−109 · php +495/−98 · md +30/−11
  • Diff: 5403b87
  • Discussion: #3586706 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The Duplicate action on AI Context items now always creates a draft copy, for every user and whether or not "Publish by default" is on. Before, a user who could not use the Publish transition could still get a published copy, which skipped editorial review. The copy is also now owned by the user who duplicated it, gets new created and changed dates, and keeps neither the original's publishing schedule nor its revision log message. A user without the "Create new draft" transition now gets a form error instead of a copy. At the global item limit, duplicating a global item now saves a draft and shows no error, because the limit is checked when the copy is published. Sites running earlier versions should look for published items with the same label or created date as another item and review them.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Editorial workflow bypass: a user without the publish transition could get a published copy through Duplicate when Publish by default was on. Needs restricted permissions (Create and Edit AI Context Item).
  • Permission change: Duplicate now requires the use ai_context_editorial transition create_new_draft permission. Users without it get a form error, even if they may publish.

Technical details

The cause was in AiContextItemDuplicateForm::buildDuplicate(). It set the published status and the published moderation state from default_status, and validateForm() only ran the module persistence rules, never entity validation. So Content Moderation's ModerationState constraint never checked the transition. Now buildDuplicate() always produces a draft, using the new setDuplicateState() to call setUnpublished() and set moderation_state to draft on every translation. createDuplicate() copies all translations, but the route only passes the one in the current content language. validateForm() also calls ->validate() on the moderation_state field and turns each violation into a form error. A new item is checked as a transition from the workflow's initial state, so the user needs the Create new draft transition.

buildDuplicate() also resets fields that described the original. The RESET_FIELDS constant (uid, created, changed, publish_on, publish_state, unpublish_on, unpublish_state) gets applyDefaultValue() on each translation, since created and changed are translatable. The revision creation time and log message are reset through the entity type's revision metadata keys. The revision user is set to NULL so that AiContextItem::preSave() falls back to the owner. getDefaultStatus() and the config factory constructor argument are removed, and getDescription() always returns "A new draft copy will be created." The description of "Publish by default" in AiContextItemSettingsForm now says Duplicate always creates a draft. The docs are updated, including the removal of references to a "Duplicate tab". Kernel tests (AiContextItemDuplicateFormTest, new AiContextItemDuplicateScheduleTest) and functional tests in AiContextItemListTest were updated or added.

Upgrade

Grant use ai_context_editorial transition create_new_draft (AI Context editorial workflow: Use Create new draft transition) to any role that should keep using Duplicate. Copies made before this fix keep the original's label and created date, so check for published items sharing a label or created date with another item. This check also finds legitimate copies made by users who could publish.

item.title: #3586702: Usage records keep every request path with no limit on number or length
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +471/−30 · php +417/−27 · md +53/−3 · yml +1
  • Diff: fd64e41
  • Discussion: #3586702 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

With usage tracking on, a user who could send requests to a push consumer (for example a chatbot) could make a usage record grow without limit by sending a different, very long path in each request. That slowed AI requests for everyone using the consumer and could make them fail. Each usage record now keeps only the last 20 request paths, each at most 255 characters, and a client-supplied path hint longer than 2,048 characters is ignored. Errors from usage tracking during agent runs are now logged and no longer fail the run. Usage tracking is off by default. A record saved before the update is cut the next time a path is added to it. A record already too large to load is not cut and must be cleared.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Unbounded growth of usage record routes from client-supplied paths could slow or break AI requests of a push consumer for all users (denial of service, no data exposure); usage tracking is off by default.

Technical details

The new AiContextUsage::setRoutes() drops empty and non-string values, truncates each path to MAX_ROUTE_LENGTH (255) characters with Unicode::truncate() and an ellipsis, moves repeated paths to the end, and stores only the last MAX_ROUTES (20). addRoute() now delegates to it, so a repeated path moves to the end instead of keeping its first position. In AiContextUsageTracker::attachEntity(), the old record's routes are merged first (setRoutes(array_merge(old, current))), so the limit drops the oldest paths and keeps the run's. A new record for another entity gets its first path through addRoute(), so the limits apply there too.

AiContextRequestInfoResolver::normalizeSuppliedPath() returns NULL when the path, after the query string and fragment are removed, is longer than MAX_PATH_LENGTH (2048) characters (mb_strlen()). setPath() then returns FALSE and getPath() falls through to the next source, ending at the request path, which has no limit of its own.

AiContextAgentToolSubscriber::onToolFinished() wraps recordToolUsed(), extractEntityInfo() and attachEntity() in a try block. AiContextAgentFinishedSubscriber::onAgentFinished() does the same for flushToolsUsed(). Both catch Throwable and log an error naming the runner ID. AiContextAgentFinishedSubscriber gets a LoggerInterface as its second constructor argument, wired to @logger.channel.ai_context in ai_context.services.yml. A PHP memory-limit error is fatal and is not a Throwable, so the path limits are the main fix and the try/catch is a second safeguard. No update hook is added. All changed classes are @internal.

Upgrade

If a consumer already fails because of oversized usage records, turn off usage tracking at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/usage, then clear the records at /admin/config/ai/context/settings/usage/clear. If the clear page also fails, empty the table and rebuild the caches:

drush sql:query "TRUNCATE TABLE ai_context_usage"
drush cr

item.title: #3586701: Core "view any unpublished content" permission shows unpublished context items
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +217/−9 · php +174/−9 · md +43
  • Diff: 94b0dbc
  • Discussion: #3586701 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

Users whose role had core's "View any unpublished content" permission, such as the Content editor role on Drupal CMS, could read draft and archived AI Context items even with no AI Context permission. This included the item page, the Latest version tab, revision pages, and the CCC listing for roles that also had "View AI Context Items in CCC". After the fix, unpublished items are visible only to users with "Administer AI Context", "View any unpublished AI Context Item", or the owner holding "View AI Context Items in CCC". Roles that need to see drafts must be given "View any unpublished AI Context Item". Published items are unchanged. Run drush cr after updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Access bypass: core's "View any unpublished content" (via Content Moderation) let users read draft and archived context items without any AI Context permission. Affects 1.0.0-beta1 to 1.0.0-rc1 and 1.0.x.
  • API change: view access on an unpublished context item is now forbidden, not neutral, when no context item rule allows it, so hook_entity_access() and hook_ai_context_item_access() implementations can no longer grant it.

Technical details

AiContextItemAccessControlHandler::checkAccess() returned a neutral result for view of an unpublished item when no rule matched. Content Moderation's hook_entity_access() allows view of any unpublished entity for "view any unpublished content", and a neutral result let that grant win. The handler now returns AccessResult::forbidden() in that case, because a forbidden result cannot be overridden by other access hooks. Cache metadata is kept: a non-owner with view ai context items gets a forbidden result with per-permissions and per-user contexts. A user without that permission gets a forbidden result per permissions only, since ownership does not matter, plus the item as a cacheable dependency. Published items still return neutral.

Because the check is on entity view access, it also covers the routes that depend on it: the Latest version tab still needs core's "View the latest version" and "View any unpublished content" but now also needs view access to the item. The revision history and revision pages need the revision permission plus view access to each revision. Kernel tests in AiContextItemModerationAccessTest and AiContextItemAccessControlHandlerCacheTest cover these routes and the cache contexts. Docs were updated in access-boundaries.md, configuration.md and api-stability.md.

Upgrade

Roles that must see draft or archived context items (including editors who save a new draft and are redirected to the Latest version tab) need the "View any unpublished AI Context Item" permission. Without it the Latest version tab now shows "Access denied", though the save still works. Custom hook_entity_access() or hook_ai_context_item_access() code can no longer allow view of unpublished items. Run drush cr after updating.

item.title: #3586696: Add the load_ai_context_items function call and deprecate load_ai_context_item_by_id
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +886/−268 · php +779/−249 · md +107/−19
  • Diff: 65f20b7
  • Discussion: #3586696 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The AI Context load tool has a new ID, ai_context:load_ai_context_items, because the old name load_ai_context_item_by_id did not match what the tool does (it loads one or more items) or the other two tool IDs. The new tool has the same inputs, access checks and output as before. The old ID stays as a deprecated alias until 2.0.0, so existing agents keep working. The agent tool list shows it as "Load AI Context Item By ID (deprecated)". New agents should use the new tool. Existing agent configuration is not migrated automatically. Agent prompts that name the old tool must be edited by hand.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Agent configuration that names the old plugin ID (tools, default information tools, overrides) keeps working but should be changed by hand to the new ID. No update hook migrates it.
  • Deprecation: Function call plugin ID ai_context:load_ai_context_item_by_id is deprecated in 1.0.0 and removed in 2.0.0. Each call triggers E_USER_DEPRECATED.
  • New API: New function call plugin ID ai_context:load_ai_context_items (function name ai_context_load_ai_context_items, tool name "Load AI Context Items").

Technical details

The load logic moved out of LoadAiContextItemById into a new @internal abstract base class, AiContextLoadItemsFunctionCallBase. The new LoadAiContextItems plugin extends it with no overrides. LoadAiContextItemById also extends it, keeps its old id and function_name, and changes its name and description to say it is deprecated and name the new ID. Its execute() calls @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) and then parent::execute(). The notice fires only when the tool runs. Listing the tools, building the agent form or creating the plugin does not trigger it. Both #[FunctionCall] attributes carry the same context_definitions, and the class docblock says to keep them in sync.

The docs (docs/developers/api-stability.md, function_calls.md, index.md, services.md) now use the new ID. api-stability.md lists the alias under "Deprecated APIs" and has an "Upgrade from 1.0.0-rc1: Load tool plugin ID" section. That section says to change default_information_tools entries and agent overrides to the new ID. It also says usage records still show the old ID for agents that have not been moved. A new kernel test, AiContextLoadFunctionCallAliasTest, checks that the definitions match, the output is identical for both IDs including the permission denial, and the deprecation fires only on execute. AiContextEchoAiSystemPromptTest gains a case that runs the old ID as a default information tool.

Upgrade

Replace the old plugin ID in agent config, using the same parameters:

tool: ai_context:load_ai_context_item_by_id

becomes

tool: ai_context:load_ai_context_items

This applies to the agent's tool selection and tool settings, its Default information tools, and any AI Agents agent overrides. Agent prompts that mention ai_context:load_ai_context_item_by_id or ai_context_load_ai_context_item_by_id must be edited by hand to use ai_context:load_ai_context_items or ai_context_load_ai_context_items. To find agents that still use the old ID, check the Tools used list on usage records.
